clue.text: What falls easily to one as a Northerner?

definitions.text: What falls easily to one as a Northerner?

parts.words: What falls easily to one as a Northerner?
parts.note: something that falls into your lap comes easily; split, the word for a native of the far north reads as a thing that lands in a lap

explanation.surface: A riddle about what comes easily to someone from the far north.
explanation.walkthrough: Split the answer as LAP LANDER: something that lands in your lap has fallen to you easily. Lapland is the Arctic region spanning northern Scandinavia and Finland.
explanation.definitionFit: A native of Lapland, in the Arctic north of Scandinavia, is literally a Northerner.

clue.text: Leggy stripper fails to keep bottom in position

indicators.note: the bottom of a down entry is its last letter, which is not kept

parts.note: a locust is a long-legged insect that strips crops bare

explanation.surface: A long-legged exotic dancer can't keep her bottom in place.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Leggy stripper' suggests a dancer; it is the crop-stripping insect.
explanation.definitionFit: A locus is a place or position, especially in mathematics for a set of points.

clue.text: Fuss over second-rate culinary plant

indicators.note: over puts the fuss above the grade letter in a down entry

parts.note: a pother is a fuss or commotion
B is the second grade, second-rate

explanation.surface: A fuss is made over a mediocre kitchen herb.
explanation.definitionFit: A pot herb is any plant grown for cooking, such as parsley or a leafy green.

clue.text: Caught girl in her underwear under a bit of a spell?

indicators.note: under places the rest below the single letter in a down entry
in sets the caught girl between the underwear pieces

parts.note: bras, a woman's underwear, taken as a pair of bras
C is the cricket abbreviation for caught
Ada is a girl's name

explanation.surface: A girl caught in her underwear, under a spell of sorts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'her underwear' is taken as plural, a bra either side of the caught girl; 'under' puts it all below A in this down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: The magician's incantation is a word from a spell, so 'a bit of a spell' with a question mark.

clue.text: Fuel drops fell away from casing

parts.note: dies means drops, as a wind dies or drops

indicators.note: the casing of a word is its outer letters, taken away to leave the middle

explanation.surface: Fuel drips fell from a container.
explanation.definitionFit: Diesel is the heavy oil fuel burned in diesel engines.

clue.text: Wine store raided by old fighter pilot

parts.note: red is red wine

indicators.note: raided by means broken into, so the old letter goes inside the store

parts.note: a barn is a farm store

explanation.surface: An elderly flying ace raids a wine cellar.
explanation.definitionFit: Manfred von Richthofen, the Red Baron, was the top German fighter ace of the First World War.

clue.text: Opportunity to give out name woman left

indicators.note: to give something out is to let it go, so the opportunity word loses a letter here

parts.note: a window is an opportunity, a window of opportunity

explanation.surface: An opening lets a name slip, and a woman is left behind.
explanation.definitionFit: A woman whose husband has died is the one left behind, hence a woman left.

clue.text: Did live salsa with revolutionary shows

indicators.note: revolutionary means turning round, so the found letters are read backwards
shows means displays, so the letters are on view in the words salsa with

explanation.surface: Someone performed live salsa with a revolutionary at the shows.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shows' signals letters on display inside SALSA WITH; 'revolutionary' turns SAW round.
explanation.definitionFit: The past tense of 'to be' means existed, so it stands for did live.

clue.text: Mostly unattractive parts to perform in role of bloke

indicators.note: parts means separates, so the shortened word comes between the others

parts.note: to do is to perform
as means in the role of, as in 'acting as'

indicators.note: mostly means not quite all, so the last letter is dropped

parts.note: ugly means unattractive

explanation.surface: Unattractive acting roles for a man to play.
explanation.walkthrough: 'parts' looks like stage roles but is the verb 'splits apart', with the shortened ugly word splitting the other two pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Douglas is an example of a male first name, so it can stand for a bloke.

clue.text: Medic stops having beard scratched

indicators.note: stops means plugs a gap, so the medic sits between the other pieces

parts.note: with means having
an awn is the bristly beard on an ear of barley
DR is the abbreviation for doctor, a medic

explanation.surface: A doctor stops having his beard scratched.
explanation.walkthrough: 'beard' is not a man's whiskers but the awn on barley.
explanation.definitionFit: A horse that is scratched has been taken out of a race, pulled from the field.

clue.text: Set erotic novel at heart of dukedom

indicators.note: at places the central letter next to the rearranged letters
novel means new or fresh, so the letters of erotic are made into something new
the heart of a word is its middle letter, here the fourth of seven

explanation.surface: A racy book sits at the centre of a ducal estate.
explanation.walkthrough: 'novel' looks like a noun for a book, but it signals a new arrangement of EROTIC to give COTERI; the heart of DUKEDOM is its central E.
explanation.definitionFit: A set is a close social circle, a clique of people sharing interests.

clue.text: Turn off grand, posh thoroughfare following police officers

indicators.note: following puts the grand, posh street letters after the officers

parts.note: DIs are detective inspectors, police officers
G is slang shorthand for a grand, a thousand pounds
U means upper-class, posh, in British usage
ST is the abbreviation for street, a thoroughfare

explanation.surface: Something about a grand, smart avenue behind the police repels someone.
explanation.walkthrough: U for upper-class comes from the 1950s British 'U and non-U' debate on posh speech.
explanation.definitionFit: To turn someone off is to repel or revolt them, a verb synonym.

clue.text: Get court witness and judge

definitions.meaning: to get it is to understand
to court someone is to date them
to witness an event is to observe it

explanation.surface: A legal instruction: secure a courtroom witness and a judge.
explanation.definitionFit: The three-letter verb covers understanding, dating, observing and assessing, each a sense of these four words.

clue.text: Course supplement given by Classics masters to a boy?

parts.note: the Caesars were the emperors, masters of the classical Roman world
a lad is a boy

explanation.surface: Classics teachers hand out extra coursework to a pupil.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Classics masters' suggests schoolteachers, but it means the Roman emperors; read as CAESAR'S A LAD.
explanation.definitionFit: A salad dressed with Caesar dressing accompanies or supplements a meal's course.

clue.text: Put up with a kid giving one an order

parts.note: to stand something is to put up with it
to kid is to tease

explanation.surface: Tolerating a child who issues one with commands.
explanation.walkthrough: 'kid' looks like a child but is the verb to tease.
explanation.definitionFit: On parade, a drill sergeant's command lets troops relax, an order given to soldiers.

clue.text: Give form to doctor to fill in years after drug overdose

indicators.note: to fill in is to occupy a gap, so the doctor letters go inside the others
after places the years letter behind the drug and overdose letters

parts.note: E is short for ecstasy, the drug
MB is Bachelor of Medicine, a doctor's qualification

explanation.surface: A doctor steps in years after a patient's drug overdose.
explanation.definitionFit: To embody an idea is to give it a concrete, physical form.

clue.text: Husband breaking into taxes due after change is all spent

indicators.note: breaking into means forcing a way inside, so the husband letter goes in
after change means the letters of taxes due are rearranged

explanation.surface: A husband dips into money owed in tax and finds it all gone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'after change' rearranges TAXES DUE to EXAUSTED, and 'breaking into' puts H inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Being totally drained of energy or supplies is to be used up, all spent.

clue.text: Place for sailing and swimming race, also

indicators.note: swimming suggests the letters are swirling about, so the race word and the last word are rearranged

parts.note: the page smudges this word between its a and o; the eight-letter count and the anagram show it is also

explanation.surface: A spot fit for both yachting and a swimming contest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'swimming race' reads as one event, but swimming is the anagram signal for RACE ALSO.
explanation.definitionFit: The Coral Sea, off north-east Australia, is a body of water where ships sail.

clue.text: Coin not necessarily found in lead pipe

parts.note: a rein is a lead for a horse
a vent is a pipe or outlet for air

explanation.surface: A coin that may not turn up inside a lead pipe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Coin' looks like money but is the verb to invent; to coin anew is to make up again something that was not necessarily found before.
explanation.definitionFit: To devise something afresh, making it again from scratch, is to coin it anew.

clue.text: Instant reflection in language a product of the domestic press?

definitions.text: a product of the domestic press?

indicators.note: in places the turned instant inside the language

parts.note: Hebrew is the language of Israel

indicators.note: a reflection shows a thing back to front, so the instant word is read backwards

parts.note: a mo is an instant, a moment

explanation.surface: A quick thought in some tongue, about what a home press turns out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'press' suggests newspapers, but it is a wine or cider press at home.
explanation.definitionFit: Drink made at home, pressed and fermented in a kitchen, comes from a domestic press, hence the question mark.

clue.text: Maiden Man Ray shot in Far East location

parts.note: M is the abbreviation for maiden, a cricket over with no runs

indicators.note: shot means wrecked or ruined, so the letters are broken up and rearranged

explanation.surface: The photographer Man Ray takes a picture of a young woman somewhere in Asia.
explanation.walkthrough: Man Ray was the American Surrealist photographer, so 'shot' suggests a photograph.
explanation.definitionFit: Myanmar, formerly Burma, is a country in South-East Asia, part of the Far East.

clue.text: Pioneering American's time at Twickenham recalled

indicators.note: recalled means called back, so the rugby call is read backwards

parts.note: in rugby union, no side is the referee's call ending the match; Twickenham is England's rugby stadium

explanation.surface: An American trailblazer's moment at the rugby ground is remembered.
explanation.walkthrough: Twickenham is the home of English rugby, where 'no side' calls time on a match; 'recalled' turns it round. The 's stands for 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: Thomas Edison, inventor of the phonograph and light bulb, was a pioneering American inventor.

clue.text: One's big hits the result of great toil?

definitions.meaning: a batsman who hits big shots with little finesse in cricket
one who slogs works hard, so great toil makes such a worker

explanation.definitionFit: A batsman given to wild big hits is one, and so is a hard grafter who toils.

clue.text: Inch away from fire as the smoke starts rising

indicators.note: rising in a down entry means the letters are read from the bottom up
the starts of words are their first letters, taken from each of six words

explanation.surface: Inching away from a fire as the smoke goes up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Inch' looks like a measure but is the Scottish word for a small island; Staffa, in the Inner Hebrides, is famous for Fingal's Cave.
explanation.definitionFit: In Scotland an inch is a small island, and this one lies off Mull in the Hebrides.

clue.text: Struggling university secretary gets the bird

parts.note: a PA, personal assistant, is a secretary
gains means gets
a tit is a small bird

explanation.surface: A college secretary in difficulty gets a bird, or gets jeered.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gets the bird' is an idiom for being booed, but here 'gets' and 'the bird' are two separate pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone facing serious difficulty, in a tough spot, is in a struggling situation; it is an idiom.

clue.text: Dorothy skipped and retained throughout an expression of delight

indicators.note: letters are alternately skipped and kept along the whole name, taking the second, fourth and sixth

explanation.surface: Dorothy skipped along, keeping it up, with a happy cry.
explanation.walkthrough: Dorothy skipping down the yellow brick road is the picture; the instruction is to skip one letter and keep the next.
explanation.definitionFit: A cry of pleasure or wonder is the classic exclamation of delight.

clue.text: Hard breathing after removing one's tie

indicators.note: after places the shortened word behind the hard letter

parts.note: H is the abbreviation for hard, as on pencils

indicators.note: removing means taking out, so the one letter is dropped

parts.note: alive means still breathing
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Heavy breathing after undoing one's necktie.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tie' looks like a necktie but is a drawn result; the 's stands for 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: In golf, to share a hole with the same score is a tie, a drawn hole.

clue.text: Dish from party returned within the hour

indicators.note: within puts the turned party inside the hour word

parts.note: the hour is the time, as in 'what time is it?'

indicators.note: returned means sent back, so the party is read backwards

parts.note: Lab is short for Labour, the British political party

explanation.surface: A dish arrives from a party, sent back within the hour.
explanation.definitionFit: A timbale is a drum-shaped mould dish of meat or fish, baked and turned out.

clue.text: Fifty per cent of pitch in sap

indicators.note: fifty per cent is half, so the second half of the helping word is dropped

parts.note: to pitch in is to help, assist

explanation.surface: Half the pitch is found in tree sap.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pitch' and 'sap' suggest tree resins, but pitch in means help and a sap is a fool.
explanation.definitionFit: A sap is a gullible fool, and so is a donkey in slang.

clue.text: Irishman's dread when meeting female

indicators.note: when meeting joins the two pieces side by side

parts.note: fear is dread
a gal is a girl, a female

explanation.surface: An Irishman's terror when he has to meet a woman.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's stands for 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: Feargal is a traditional Irish male given name, borne by many Irishmen.

clue.text: Shoots game

definitions.meaning: the pub game of throwing arrows at a board

explanation.definitionFit: The word means quick dashes, as in shooting across a room, and names the pub game of throwing at a board.

clue.text: Partly touching tip of tongue on amphibian, say

indicators.note: on means placed after, so the touching letters follow the amphibian ones

parts.note: a toad is an amphibian
say means for example, abbreviated EG
re means about, touching on

indicators.note: the tip of a word here is its final letter, its end

explanation.surface: A toad's sticky tongue, partly touching what it catches.
explanation.walkthrough: The tip of 'tongue' is its last letter, E, not its first.
explanation.definitionFit: Something true only partly is true in some measure; an idiom for 'somewhat'.
